title: Feed thirty users from one pool
briefing: Same 4×80 GB box: 180 GB of cache pool after weights. Demand is rising and product wants **30 concurrent users at 16K+ context**, served stably (don't redline the pool). Your naive allocator only makes 40% of the pool usable. The knobs are demand, context — and the allocator itself.
debrief: 30 users × 16K × 320 KB ≈ 100+ GB of real tokens — physically fine in 180 GB, impossible when the allocator wastes 60%. The only winning move is the **usable-pool knob: go paged**. That slider is PagedAttention: fixed-size blocks, allocated as tokens land, one shared pool. Capacity you already paid for, returned by software.
